findings.highlight: since you seemed down this morning.
findings.evidenceJa: 朝から体調悪そうだったから
findings.governingReading: Shirou came because Sakura had appeared physically unwell since morning.
findings.explanation: “Seemed down” makes Shirou's stated reason less clearly about physical illness. The surrounding English still describes Sakura as unwell.

findings.highlight: You didn't put any weight into your step.
findings.evidenceJa: 足、ぜんぜんふんばりきいてないじゃないか
findings.governingReading: ふんばりきいてない describes an involuntary lack of bodily support after a mere hand-grab nearly topples her.
findings.explanation: Sakura’s legs being unable to brace or hold firm becomes her failing to put weight into a step.

findings.highlight: I never have any reply to that look.
findings.evidenceJa: そんな顔でそんな風に言われたら、言い返す事もできなくなる。
findings.governingReading: そんな顔でそんな風に言われたら is conditional and local to Sakura’s present subdued appeal about Shinji.
findings.explanation: Shirou being unable to answer this particular look and phrasing becomes never having any reply to that look.

findings.highlight: my words will fall on deaf ears. Anything I said would just seem like unnecessary meddling.
findings.evidenceJa: 部外者の無責任な言葉にすぎないんだから。
findings.governingReading: He limits himself because however much he thinks of Sakura as family, what he says about the Matou family would still be the irresponsible words of an outsider.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s fear that an outsider’s words would be irresponsible becomes a prediction that nobody will listen and that he would merely meddle.

findings.highlight: Sakura reluctantly sits on the chair.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜はしずしずと椅子に座った。
findings.governingReading: しずしずと describes restrained, decorous movement; it does not state opposition to sitting after she yields.
findings.explanation: Sakura sitting down quietly and demurely becomes sitting reluctantly.

findings.highlight: Drinking tea in the classroom is good for you once in a while.
findings.evidenceJa: 教室で茶を飲むってのも一度ぐらいはいいもんだ
findings.governingReading: 一度ぐらいはいいもんだ recommends the unusual experience on this occasion, as part of Shirou’s small rule-breaking care.
findings.explanation: Drinking tea in the classroom once as an enjoyable novelty becomes something medically or generally “good for you” once in a while.

findings.highlight: Sakura wouldn't have had to interact with me at all really.
findings.evidenceJa: 桜が衛宮士郎という先輩を持つ事もなかった
findings.governingReading: The source describes the contingent formation of a valued senpai relationship, not an obligation she otherwise could avoid.
findings.explanation: Without Shinji, Sakura would never have had Shirou as her senior becomes her not having had to interact with him.

findings.highlight: I sneak a glace at Sakura.
findings.governingReading: Shirou steals a look at Sakura’s profile.

findings.highlight: On top of that, she's sensible, and so gentle.
findings.evidenceJa: くわえてよく気が利いて、性格も穏やかだ。
findings.governingReading: よく気が利いて describes noticing needs and acting considerately, central to her household care.
findings.explanation: Sakura’s attentiveness to others becomes being sensible.

findings.highlight: Four years ago, when I'd just started school.
findings.evidenceJa: 四年前、わたしが進学したばかりの頃です。
findings.governingReading: 進学したばかり situates the four-years-ago memory just after her progression into the new school, not the beginning of education.
findings.explanation: Sakura having just advanced into a new level of school becomes having only just started school at all.

findings.highlight: They would run, jump, drop their pole, and repeat that step.
findings.evidenceJa: 走って、跳んで、棒を落として、また繰り返して。
findings.governingReading: The person is doing 走り高跳び. 棒 is the horizontal bar: he runs, jumps, knocks it down, and cannot clear a bar set above his own height.
findings.explanation: The high-jump bar is repeatedly turned into a pole, shifting Sakura’s formative memory toward pole vaulting.

findings.highlight: they were stubborn enough not to give up.
findings.evidenceJa: なら負けないぞって意地を張ってただけなんです。
findings.governingReading: なら負けないぞって意地を張って frames him as entering a contest with the impossible task and refusing defeat, whatever the task happens to be.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s refusal to be beaten by whatever impossible thing he encountered is reduced to generic stubbornness about not giving up.

findings.governingReading: オチてない comments on narrative payoff after he wrongly expects successful clearance; it is a comic response to Sakura’s anti-climax.
findings.explanation: Shirou saying the story has no punchline becomes saying it lacks a happy ending.

findings.highlight: embarrassed that she saw me in such an awkward moment.
findings.evidenceJa: つまんないモン見られたなあ
findings.governingReading: つまんないモン dismisses what Sakura saw as trivial or unimpressive, consistent with his inability to value his own effort.
findings.explanation: Shirou calls the witnessed effort a boring or worthless thing; the English calls it an awkward moment.

findings.highlight: you don't have to worry about taking the time to go to my house tonight.
findings.evidenceJa: 無理してうちに来なくていい
findings.governingReading: 無理してうちに来なくていい is grounded in her physical condition and tells her not to overextend herself.
findings.explanation: Shirou telling still-unwell Sakura not to force herself to come over becomes telling her not to worry about taking the time.
